scenario.name: Sandworm HermeticWiper Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) MBR & NTFS $MFT Destruction
scenario.overview: Imagine a wartime saboteur who is not after ransom money at all, but wants every computer in an organization turned into a permanent brick before sunrise. First, the saboteur unpacks an authentic, validly signed disk-partitioning guard badge from its own coat pocket to gain direct physical access to the raw floor tiles; next, it disables every backup and crash log while shattering the building index directory; finally, it smashes the front entrance map of every hard drive with pure random static so no floor can ever start up again. In this scenario (T1068, Sandworm HermeticWiper Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) MBR & NTFS $MFT Destruction), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: extracting, then disabling Volume Shadow Copy , Crash Dumps, then raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Extracting, then Disabling Volume Shadow Copy , Crash Dumps, then Raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 6 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Extracting & Registering Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) from RCDATA
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation & Defense Evasion (T1068 / T1543.003)
stages.description: Pushed simultaneously across hundreds of offices by the central policy board, the saboteur unlocks special driver-loading clearance, pulls an authentic signed disk-utility driver out of its own hidden pocket, and bolts it straight into the building core engine. Upon execution via Active Directory GPO or WMI, HermeticWiper enabled SeLoadDriverPrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, and SeShutdownPrivilege in its process token, checked the OS architecture and Windows version, decompressed an MSZIP-compressed resource (DRV_X64 / DRV_XP_X64) from its PE RCDATA section into C:\Windows\System32\drivers\<2_random_chars>dr.sys (a legitimate, Microsoft-signed copy of empntdrv.sys from EaseUS Partition Master), and loaded it into the kernel. Both the outer HermeticWiper executable (signed by Hermetica Digital Ltd until revoked) and the inner empntdrv.sys kernel driver (signed by CHENGDU YIWO Tech Development Co., Ltd.) carried valid Authenticode signatures at the time of the attack. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Stage 1: Extracting & Registering Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) from RCDATA / ⇠#1 ACK 6) from Node ① (#1 Sandworm GPO / WMI Deployment) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PhysicalDrive0 MBR & NTFS $MFT Wiped).

stages.title: Stage 2: Disabling Volume Shadow Copy (vss), Crash Dumps & Fragmenting NTFS Metadata
stages.subtitle: Inhibit System Recovery & Defense Evasion (T1490 / T1070)
stages.description: Before swinging the sledgehammer, the saboteur pulls the power plugs on the building automatic backup vault and crash-diary recorder, then deliberately shatters the floor index catalog into thousands of broken fragments so recovery teams cannot piece files back together. HermeticWiper called ChangeServiceConfigW and ControlService to disable and stop the vss (Volume Shadow Copy) service, set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl\CrashDumpEnabled = 0 (preventing Windows from writing a MEMORY.DMP kernel crash dump when the corrupted system inevitably blue-screened, thereby denying incident responders RAM forensics), and parsed the raw NTFS boot sector and Master File Table ($MFT) to map the exact physical disk runlists of $MFT, $LogFile, $Bitmap, and C:\Windows\System32\config registry hives. By parsing the NTFS $MFT runlist fragments directly rather than using standard Windows file APIs, HermeticWiper could corrupt the exact physical sectors backing critical OS metadata even while Windows held those files locked. In the documented EventID 7040 exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica), HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica) responds with ALERT 7040 (confirming that the Stage 2: Disabling Volume Shadow Copy (vss), Crash Dumps & Fragmenting NTFS Metadata request succeeded on HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: Raw \.PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR & NTFS $MFT Overwrite with CSPRNG Bytes). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: Disabling Volume Shadow Copy (vss), Crash Dumps & Fragmenting NTFS Metadata / ⇠#2 ALERT 7040) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PhysicalDrive0 MBR & NTFS $MFT Wiped).

stages.title: Stage 3: Raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR & NTFS $MFT Overwrite with CSPRNG Bytes
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1561.002 - Disk Structure Wipe)
stages.description: Walking methodically from storage bay zero up to bay one hundred, the saboteur uses its raw disk pass to blast every drive opening directory and master file catalog with irreversible random noise, then flips the building power breaker so no machine ever boots again. Iterating through \\.\PhysicalDrive0 up to \\.\PhysicalDrive100, HermeticWiper generated cryptographically random bytes via CryptGenRandom and overwrote the Master Boot Record (MBR) (first 512 bytes of sector 0), GPT partition headers, and the mapped physical sector extents of $MFT, $LogFile, and C:\Users, before invoking ExitWindowsEx(EWX_REBOOT | EWX_FORCE) to immediately reboot the machine into an unrecoverable, unbootable state. Because the $MFT (which maps where every file resides on an NTFS volume) and $MFTMirr are overwritten with random bytes from CryptGenRandom, carving or recovering filesystem structure is rendered impossible in seconds without having to overwrite every gigabyte of the disk. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: Raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR & NTFS $MFT Overwrite with CSPRNG Bytes / ⇠#3 ALERT T1561.002) from Node ③ (#3 HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica)) to Node ④ (#4 Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PhysicalDrive0 MBR & NTFS $MFT Wiped).
